history.dynasty: Portuguese colonial era (deity relocated from Margao in 1567)
history.period: Original Margao temple predated the 16th century; current complex at Zambaulim established after 1567
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 226 / Shree Damodar Temple (Zambaulim) — this CSV row appears to refer to the same real temple. Dedicated to Lord Damodar, an incarnation of Shiva. The deity was originally enshrined in a temple at Mathagam (Margao), where the Holy Spirit Church now stands. During the Portuguese temple-destruction campaign in Sasashti Taluka in 1567, the mahajans shifted the deities of Damodar, Ramnath, Laxmi-Narayan, Chamundeshwari, Mahakali and Mahesh to Zambaulim, where the Desais of Rivona gave them land. The Kushawati River flowing beside the temple is regarded as sacred and believed to have healing properties. CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the temple is at Zambaulim, Quepem taluka, about 22 km from Margao — not in Margao town.

name: Damodar Temple (Saal)
town_description: Zambaulim is a small village in Quepem taluka of South Goa, set on the banks of the sacred Kushawati River. The village is best known for the Shri Damodar Sansthaan temple complex, which draws devotees of both Hindu and Catholic faiths. Surrounded by green paddy fields and laterite terrain typical of inland Goa, it lies about 22 km east of Margao.

travel.railway: Margao (Madgaon) railway station, about 22 km; Balli station is closer (verify)
travel.road: Off NH66, turning northeast towards Fatorpa/Zambaulim; regular buses run from the Margao bus stand
